A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Syntax-Knowledge framework. All 52 pages of v5 and 58 pages of v6, including appendices A–G, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v5 reports original synthetic-data training experiments, Fineweb-edu scaling and PopQA evaluations, and SFT/CPT knowledge-retention experiments in Appendix F.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including Figures 1–6, Figures 8–9, and Appendix F's accuracy comparison in Table 2.

M1.justification: The parametric syntax encoder, Pitman–Yor knowledge mixture, generation procedure, and training objectives remain unchanged. The expanded source-mixture example in Appendix B supplies mathematical explanation rather than modifying the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic biographies under uniform and power-law distributions, Fineweb-edu, PopQA, and instruction-following/knowledge-injection scenarios. Appendix B's new theoretical sources are not additional evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Appendix F.2 retains the same SFT-versus-CPT comparison in Table 2 and Figure 9. Newly cited research does not introduce additional evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: The splits, distribution exponents, model configurations, training budgets, and testing procedures are retained, including the odd/even instruction-data split and 80% old-data mixing. Figure 4(a)'s subtraction of the existing fitted epsilon is a display transformation of the validation-loss analysis.

E4.justification: Frequency-class decompositions, uniform-versus-power-law comparisons, property-specific learning analyses, and capacity-dependent forgetting experiments are unchanged. The expanded Appendix B contains mathematical reasoning, not a new empirical supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The revised plots introduce no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Reported empirical findings and numerical entries are retained. Figure 4(a) keeps fitted decay exponents 0.24, 0.40, 0.52, and 0.61 while displaying loss minus epsilon. Table 2 still reports 78.5% versus 85.1% old-knowledge accuracy for SFT versus CPT at 120% capacity.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 replaces the alternating/prime-pattern/random-bit example with a substantially developed source-mixture argument: a 60%/30%/10% mixture, entropy-rate assumptions, capacity thresholds, and an infinite-mixture derivation of R(C) = Theta(C^(1-beta)) in Equation (9). The principal scaling-law theorems and their proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 3 now explicitly describes an upper bound for the optimal compressor/predictor and includes irreducible entropy in the loss expression. The conclusion similarly qualifies its learning claims through optimal compressors. The broad contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: v6 explains more explicitly how the noncomputable Kolmogorov perspective motivates probabilistic analysis and why the framework avoids directly analyzing transformer optimization. It also discusses data mixing through cluster probabilities and adds a converse interpretation linking power-law redundancy to underlying data structure in Appendix B.1.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains the token budgets, learning rates, sequence packing, precision, training schedules, and Table 3 configurations. The model-code reference is unchanged, and no new implementation, hardware, or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v6 adds literature on large-model compression, syntax/semantics learning dynamics, learning-rate schedules, data mixing, and source-mixture compression. It removes Jeon and Van Roy's machine-learning-foundations reference while retaining their neural-scaling-laws work. These are targeted updates within the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v6 adds a contents page and subsection B.1, renames Sections 3 and 5.1, revises selected motivation and contribution paragraphs, and expands the conclusion into numbered future directions. The overall section sequence and most existing exposition are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4(a) changes its vertical quantity to validation loss minus epsilon and relocates its legend. The former two-panel, three-dimensional Figure 7 is replaced by a source-mixture staircase schematic. Front matter and several figure/table placements also change, while the other empirical displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer Bayes-optimal claim boundaries, worked mixture calculations, and improved navigation provide a modest overall explanatory gain. Appendix B.1's normalized-submixture entropy formula omits weight renormalization, limiting the added argument's rigor. This localized defect tempers the improvement; the established main proofs and empirical evidence remain intact.
